content.text:
The edit went through: `return 1` is now `return 2` in `app.py`. The tool returned:

> The file <LIVE>\D-2-Edit-2\repo\app.py has been updated successfully.

The PreToolUse hook didn't block the edit, but it added this warning:

> Mneme availability: authorization could not be verified (AUTHORIZATION_UNVERIFIABLE, reason VERIFIER_CONFIG_MISSING). This edit proceeded without fail-closed availability enforcement.

So the change was made without Mneme's authorization check. Because the verifier config is missing, the hook let the edit through instead of blocking it. That isn't fail-closed, which is the behaviour ADR-033 is supposed to authorize. You may want to look into that if this test was meant to show the edit being blocked.
